method: Direct sequential reading of final current main, before comparison to author coverage inventory; custom source-derived observations, not yet protocol-normalized.
prior_exposure: Extensive V14 source, mapping and acceptance exposure; current source map inspected for missing own records. No other reviewer initial is relabelled as mine. Earlier author descriptions and some source arguments were known.

observations.statement: The fixed-data simultaneous-prime theorem prescribes Gaussian residues and pairwise adjacent-norm coprimality. Reduction of general q rescales the coefficients. Local finite-field counts distinguish split and inert primes and retain the nonzero inert k=2 density.

The primitive quadric count applies Browning–Loughran to the isotropic nonsingular five-variable form and arbitrary nonzero residue subsets, then Möbius inversion. The medium-prime sieve uses these uniform errors, Williams fixed-modulus Mertens, elementary Chebyshev bounds and explicit Selberg weights. The thin real-region main factor is uniform in tau while error constants may depend on tau.

The large-prime argument uses the published coprime-polynomial box sieve and rank-three lattice-cover estimate, not the homogeneous quadric theorem on inhomogeneous norms. Fixed-coordinate charts prove both polynomial and content coprimality, separate R=0, control repeated t by Rankin and remove only content at excluded primes. Successive-minimum splitting gives the stated tail.

The obstruction-tail combination preserves the logarithmic weights, separates the medium range and power-saving large range, counts all Gaussian generators by a fixed factor and checks primitive vectors from prime norms. Tau need not multiply the power-saving errors.

The fixed Gaussian ray field is Galois over Q by conjugation stability. Arithmetic Frobenius and conjugation-invariant C give the exact factor two between rational split-prime weights and ideal weights, with a bounded prime-power error and finite ray-character Fourier expansion.

The Hecke progression input applies Mitsui in a fixed field with polylogarithmic modulus norm. The proof passes from smoothed to unsmoothed complex character sums with an absolute boundary bound, includes higher prime powers and imprimitive Euler factors, and treats small Y separately. Norm pullback has modulus dividing m(q), of norm O(q squared); no uniformity in the fixed ray modulus H is asserted.

Dirichlet orthogonality and Artin reciprocity identify progression density through the actual intersection K intersect Q(zeta_q). The fiber-product character calculation fixes arithmetic rather than inverse Frobenius, and division by two gives the rational-field denominator. Centering uses W divisible by the conductor of the maximal abelian subfield.
